name: Ferraxon
description: A vasoactive-synthetic compound that floods chrome-tissue interfaces with an accelerant neurotransmitter analog, temporarily pushing mechanical augments 40-60% beyond their rated performance envelope. Users report their augmented limbs feeling 'alive' — faster, stronger, more responsive than the hardware should allow. The effect is real: firmware governors are chemically bypassed, and the chrome simply runs hot.
effects: Augmented limb strength increased 40-60% above rated spec
Reflex augments operate at 1.5x design speed
Thermal vision and optical augments gain increased resolution and range
Proprioceptive feedback sharpened — augments feel more integrated with body
side_effects: Interface joint microfractures with repeated use
Hardware overheating — augments run 8-12°C above normal operating temp
Withdrawal causes augments to feel 'dead' or disconnected
Risk of actuator burnout in military-grade chrome
cultural_context: Ferraxon is the working muscle of the Shelf — laborers who need to hit harder in pit fights, couriers outrunning enforcers, fixers who can't afford a chrome upgrade but need one tonight. It's also quietly popular among Tier 2 dock workers who overload their lift-rigs to make quota. The name comes from the ferrous smell users report sweating out during the peak. Regulars are called 'spikers.'
story_hooks: A Shelf pit fighter's Ferraxon supply has been cut — someone is buying it all, and the fighter needs to find out who before their next match

A Tier 2 factory worker collapses when their arm actuator burns out mid-shift from chronic Ferraxon use — but the incident report is being buried by the foreman, who's been supplying the drug to meet production targets
A cache of military-grade Ferraxon — a stronger, cleaner formulation — surfaces on the Shelf, suggesting someone in a Tier 4 or 5 facility is running a side operation
